title: Lesson 8: How to Disciple Others
description: Someone once helped you follow Jesus. This lesson shows how to walk alongside another person the way Jesus walked with His disciples, so that what you have received keeps being passed on.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to stand firm in the armor of God. Standing firm was never meant to be a solo fight, and neither is growing. This lesson is about helping someone else grow.

blocks.title: Four Generations
blocks.text:
Paul met Timothy in the town of Lystra. He was a young disciple with a believing mother and a good name among the believers (Acts 16:1-2). Paul did not hand him a book and wish him well. He took Timothy with him. City after city, Timothy watched Paul preach, pray, suffer, and forgive. Years later Paul could write, "You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness" (2 Timothy 3:10).

Paul called him "my true child in the faith" (1 Timothy 1:2) and told another church that Timothy had served with him "as a son with a father" (Philippians 2:22). In time, Timothy was leading a church himself.

Near the end of his life, from a prison cell, Paul wrote Timothy one last letter. In one sentence he laid out the whole plan.
and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.
Count the generations in that verse: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others also. Four generations of disciples in one sentence. That is how the gospel reached you, and it is how it keeps going.
8.1 - Who has helped you grow in your faith, and what did they do that mattered most?
With Him First

Jesus had crowds, but He poured His life into a few. He chose twelve "so that they might be with him" (Mark 3:14) before He ever sent them out. They ate with Him, walked with Him, watched Him pray, and saw how He treated people. Discipleship is caught more than it is taught. It happens around a table and along the road as much as in a lesson.

Paul said the same about his own ministry: "we were ready to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves" (1 Thessalonians 2:8). You do not only pass on information. You pass on a life.
What You Pass On
One simple picture shows what you are helping another person build.

Christ is the hub, and everything turns on Him. Two spokes connect you to God: the Word and prayer. Two connect you to people: fellowship and witness. Obedience is the rim, where faith meets the road of real life. When a spoke is missing, the ride gets rough. When you disciple someone, you help them build a life that keeps rolling, and then you help them help someone else.
8.2 - Which spoke is weakest in your own life right now?
Who and How

Paul told Timothy to look for faithful people. A simple way to remember what to look for is faithful, available, and teachable. Faithful people show up and keep their word. Available people make room in their week. Teachable people are humble enough to listen, confess, and grow. You are not looking for the most impressive person you know. You are looking for someone hungry.

Start small. Jesus had twelve and was closest to three. Two to four people of the same gender, meeting every week or two, is enough. Open the Bible together and ask simple questions: What does it say? What does it mean? How will we live it? Pray for one another. Ask how each person is really doing, and check back the next time you meet. That is most of it.

Jesus also showed a simple way to pass on what you know. First the disciples watched Him. Then they helped. Then He sent them out, and they came back to tell Him what happened (Luke 9:1-10; 10:1-17). You can follow the same steps: I do, you watch. I do, you help. You do, I help. You do, I watch. Then the person you have walked with does the same for someone else.
8.3 - Who is one faithful, available, and teachable person God may be putting in front of you?
You Do Not Have to Be Finished

Most people never start because they think they need to know more first. Timothy was young, and Paul still told him to lead (1 Timothy 4:12). Paul even wrote, "Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ" (1 Corinthians 11:1). You only need to be following Jesus and willing to let someone follow along. When you do not know an answer, say so and look for it together. Being honest about your own struggles may teach more than your strengths.

And you are not alone in it. The Jesus who sent His followers to make disciples promised, "I am with you always, to the end of the age" (Matthew 28:20). He is the One who changes hearts. Your part is to show up, open the Word, pray, and love.
8.4 - What makes you hesitate to invest in someone, and what would help you take the first step?
Lesson 8 Review

Paul poured his life into Timothy, and Timothy passed it on to faithful people who taught others also. That is how the gospel reached you. Jesus shared His life with a few before He sent them, so discipleship is caught more than it is taught. Help someone build a life with Christ at the center, joined to God through the Word and prayer, joined to people through fellowship and witness, and rolling forward in obedience. Look for someone faithful, available, and teachable, start small, and remember that you do not have to be finished to begin.
In the next lesson, you will see who God puts beside you in His mission, from your own church to the ends of the earth.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
